messages:
sam: heads up — we're seeing a spike in GPU pod evictions in us-west2 starting ~01:10 UTC, looks correlated with a flurry of node conntrack drops and a bunch of pods stuck as 'Anchored'.

jules: seeing same. eviction-rate jumped ~3x for tiny-gang jobs, warmpool not absorbing. any recent rollout?

sam: no user-facing rollout. infra-bot shows many kubelet disconnects around the same time. suspect conntrack exhaustion on some rack NICs + anchored pods preventing defrag.

kai: any k8s events? can you paste the pod/node snippets?

sam: pasted short extract below — nodes alternating Ready/NotReady and a mix of taint+anchor annotations:

```
$ kubectl get pods -n infra | egrep "tiny-gang|anchor" 
tiny-gang-44b7  0/4  Pending  0  5m  (nodeAffinity=pack:high)  anchor=locked
tiny-gang-88c0  4/4  Running  0  1h  node=gc-wn-12  tolerations: gpu:present
```

$ kubectl describe node gc-wn-12 | egrep "NotReady|conntrack|taint"
NotReady: NetworkUnavailable
Kernel: conntrack table full  (nf_conntrack_max=65536)
Taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule
```

jules: conntrack table full + anchored pods = scheduler can't reshuffle to compact. when nodes flap, kube-proxy/conntrack cleanup lags -> repeated preempt/evict.

nora: what caused anchor label to be applied? is it a long-lived canary or a scheduling policy?

sam: anchor label is applied by the job-controller when gang jobs request -sticky placement (we added it for QoS last quarter). it prevents relocation during churn. that interacts badly with conntrack spikes.

kai: quick mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily relax anchor label for tiny-gang class, 2) increase conntrack on affected AMIs (sysctl), 3) add a short-lived anchor-release job to allow defrag, 4) bump warmpool for us-west2 while we stabilize. which is least risky?

jules: increasing conntrack is low-risk and quick. anchor relaxation reduces QoS guarantees though. warmpool bump costs money but buys breathing room.

nora: schedule-wise, we can roll a node kubelet config change via cluster-autoupgrade with sysctl bump to 200k conntrack and add cleanup cron on nodes. also propose a scheduler tweak: treat anchor label as 'soft-anchored' (allow preemption after Xs) — needs a small scheduler change.

sam: can we do both: sysctl bump + anchor-release job? i'll open a runbook.

kai: i'm on the sysctl AMI build. will produce a canary AMI and push to us-west2c by +30m.

infra-bot: ACTION_CREATED: ticket INFRA-1281 "conntrack bump + anchor-release experiment in us-west2" assigned to kai. ETA 2h.

jules: i'm going to run a targeted job to remove anchor label for tiny-gang in us-west2 as a quick test (non-prod only).

sam: update: removed anchor on two smallest tiny-gang jobs. scheduler rebalanced 6 pods -> dropped eviction rate ~40% in the last 4m.

nora: nice. still seeing a few nodes with kernel drops — need AMI patch otherwise we'll be back. can we accept short-term cost and warmpool bump now?

kai: warmpool bumped +50% for the region. AMI canary built (ami-anchorcank), will validate and deploy to 10% of the fleet in 1h window.

jules: followup work items: 
- make anchor label 'soft' in scheduler (PR: eng-platform repo)
- add anchor-release cron for long-running jobs when network flakiness detected
- add conntrack alert to infra dashboards (threshold 75% nf_conntrack_max)
- doc runbook for emergency anchor removal

sam: tagging folks: @kai please post AMI ID & rollout plan when ready. @nora can you draft the scheduler PR language?

kai: will do — AMI is ami-0b12c9 (canary batch 20 nodes). posting rollout steps in the ticket.

nora: i'll prototype scheduler flag (allow_anchored_preempt_after_seconds) and request a design review.

infra-bot: NOTE: incident window opened 2025-05-16T01:13Z severity=medium.

sam: thanks everyone — keep this thread for quick updates. if we see reoccurrence after AMI roll we escalate to postmortem. :eyes:
